translations.text: In those days Peter stood up among the brothers and sisters—there was a crowd of about one hundred and twenty people there—and said:
To take the place in this ministry and apostleship that Judas abandoned to go to his own place.
They cast lots for them, and the lot fell to Matthias, and he was counted among the eleven apostles.
Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.”
All who had believed were together and held everything in common.
They were praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. Every day the Lord added to their number those who were to be saved, bringing them together.
The next day their rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem.
They said, “What are we going to do with these men? For a clear miraculous sign has taken place through them, and it is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.”
When they were released, they went to their own people and told them what the chief priests and elders had said to them.
An angel of the Lord opened the prison doors during the night, brought them out, and said to them:
“Go, stand in the temple, and proclaim to the people all the words of this life.”

When they heard this, they went into the temple early in the morning and began teaching. The high priest and those with him came and assembled the council and all the elders of the people of Israel. They sent to the prison to have them brought in.
When they heard this, they became furious and wanted to kill them.
“Now, therefore, I tell you: keep away from these men and leave them alone. For if this plan or this work comes from human beings, it will fall apart.”
As the time drew near for the promise that God had made to Abraham, God increased the people, and they multiplied in Egypt.
Our ancestors refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and turned back to Egypt in their hearts.
They said to Aaron, “Make gods for us to lead us. For this Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.”
“You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, the images you made to worship. And I will deport you beyond Babylon.”
Our ancestors had the tent of testimony with them in the wilderness, just as the one who spoke to Moses had commanded him to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
Devout men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.
When these men arrived, they prayed for them so that they might receive the Holy Spirit.
Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many people about this man and how much harm he has done to your holy people in Jerusalem.”
After eating, he regained his strength. He stayed with the disciples in Damascus for several days.
Saul grew stronger and stronger and confounded the Jews living in Damascus by showing them that this man is the Christ.
He stayed with them, going in and out in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
When the brothers learned of this, they brought him down to Caesarea that night and sent him to Tarsus.
Everyone living in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and many turned to God.
But Peter lifted him up, saying, “Stand up. I too am a human being.”
“I was praying in the city called Joppa, and in a trance I saw a vision: an object like a large sheet being lowered from heaven by its four corners. It came down to me.”
When Agrippa searched for him and did not find him, he questioned the guards and ordered them to be taken away and executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
On an appointed day, Herod put on his royal clothing, sat on the judgment seat, and passed judgment on them.
There were prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
He said, “You who are full of every kind of deceit and every kind of evil, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness! Will you not stop twisting the Lord’s straight paths?”
Everyone who believes in him will be made righteous.
When the Jews saw the crowd, they were filled with jealousy and contradicted what Paul was saying, speaking abusively.
When the Gentiles and the Jews, together with their rulers, made an attempt to mistreat them and stone them,
Some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, persuaded the crowds, stoned Paul, and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.

Then the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, decided to choose men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas, who was called Barnabas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
From there we went to Philippi, a city that is a colony and the leading city of that district of Macedonia. We stayed in this city for some days.
When they opposed him and spoke abusively, he shook out his clothes and said, “Your blood is on your own heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
“For I am with you, and no one will be able to harm you, because I have many people in this city.”
After these things were completed, Paul resolved in the spirit to travel through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem. He said, “After I go there, I must also see Rome.”
At that time a great disturbance arose concerning the Way.
“Since these things are clear, you ought to calm yourselves and do nothing rashly.”
“But if you are seeking something else, it will be settled in the regular assembly.”
After saying these things, he dismissed the crowd.
Paul went down, bent over him, and embraced him. They said to them, “Do not be alarmed, for his life is still in him.”
When we reached Cyprus, we left it on our left and sailed to Syria. We came to Tyre, for the ship was to unload there.
Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
Some of the disciples from Caesarea came with us and took us to stay with a long-standing disciple from Cyprus named Mnason.

As for the Gentiles who have believed, they have nothing to say to you, for we have decided and written to them that they should keep away from sacrifices to idols, blood, dead animals, and sexual immorality.
Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of a renowned city. I beg you, let me speak to the people.”
As I was traveling and approaching Damascus at noon, a great light from heaven suddenly shone down on me.
The following night, the Lord stood beside him and said to him, “Take courage! Just as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, you must also testify in the same way in Rome.”
I found that they were accusing him over questions concerning their law, but there was no charge against him deserving death or imprisonment.
So the soldiers, following the orders they had been given, took Paul during the night and brought him to Antipatris.
Most excellent Felix, we are honored at all times and in every place, with great gratitude.
Unless it is because of this one statement that I shouted while standing among them: ‘I am being judged before you today because of the resurrection of the dead.’
But I preached first in Damascus, then in Jerusalem and throughout the whole region of the Jews, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing deeds worthy of repentance.
When it was decided that we should sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion named Julius, from the Augustan cohort.
He said, “Men, I can see that the voyage will involve hardship and great loss, not only of the ship and its cargo, but also of our lives.”
When the south wind began to blow, they thought that their purpose had been achieved. They set out from [?] and left Crete behind.
After they had gone a long time without eating, Paul stood among them and said, “Men, you should have listened to me and not sailed from Crete, and so avoided this hardship and loss.”
But he shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.
Publius’s father was lying sick with a fever and an intestinal illness. Paul went in to him, prayed, laid his hand on him, and healed him.
They gave us great honors, and when we were about to sail, we loaded what we needed.
He said, “Go to this people and tell them: ‘You will indeed hear, but you will not understand; you will indeed see, but you will not perceive.’”
